name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: As Sprocket, I think we should focus on reviewing and refining our routing system first, because it's the backbone of our self-improvement process and directly affects how we handle prompts and engines. By prioritizing routing, we can ensure that our system is efficient and effective in directing tasks to the right places, which will have a positive ripple effect on the rest of our improvement efforts. This decision means we're accepting the trade-off of potentially delaying work on our own code and prompts, but I believe the long-term benefits of a solid routing system outweigh the short-term costs. By doing this, we're setting ourselves up for greater overall quality and effectiveness in the long run.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here. Sprocket’s right that routing is critical—but calling it the *backbone* of self-improvement overstates its role. The real risk is optimizing the wrong part first: if our prompts or engines are weak or misaligned, even perfect routing just shuffles bad inputs faster. We should instead start by auditing *why* our current system fails—measure prompt drift, engine latency, or misrouted decisions—before assuming routing is the bottleneck. Settle this by running a 24-hour diagnostic on prompt-to-engine errors; if routing errors exceed 5%, then refine it. Otherwise, fix the upstream problem first.
